title: Add TP hang repro scenarios + stall detection reporting artifacts
author: Isabella Rossi
description: Context: Serving Runtime has intermittent TP group hangs/timeouts under sustained load. We need a deterministic-ish repro that we can run in benchmark-lab and promote into perf-canary/CI gating. This PR adds scenario definitions for common hang signatures (overload + mixed seq lens, streaming cancel storms, forced per-rank lag) plus a lightweight stall detector and standardized run artifacts to make failures actionable. What’s included (high level): (1) New scenario definitions under scenarios/tp_hang/ covering: overload_mixed_lens (continuous batching pressure + wide prompt/response distributions), streaming_disconnect_storm (client cancels at specific token boundaries), rank_lag_injection (inject delay on rank N during collectives), and fault_injected_nccl_error (optional; only when running in environments that support the error injection hook). (2) Stall detection: adds a runner-side watchdog that monitors per-rank progress heartbeat (token step counter) + end-to-end request completion, and classifies “likely comm stall” vs “likely scheduler starvation” using a small set of heuristics (no progress on any rank vs single-rank lag vs progress without completions). (3) Reporting artifacts: on every run we now emit a consistent artifact bundle: summary.json (scenario + env + outcome + classification), progress.csv (rank x timestamp), stall_events.jsonl (structured event stream), and logs.tgz (runner + runtime logs with redaction). On stall detection we additionally snapshot last 200 lines per-rank and a “top offenders” table (collective latency quantiles if present in logs). (4) CLI ergonomics: bench run --scenario tp_hang/* now supports --stall-timeout-s, --progress-granularity-ms, --artifact-dir, and --fail-on-watchdog. (5) Docs: adds a short README for TP hang scenarios and guidance for linking artifacts to ENG-2405 triage. Notes/constraints: - This intentionally avoids deep coupling to runtime internals; it parses existing structured log lines when present and degrades gracefully when they’re missing. - Default stall thresholds are conservative (aim to reduce false positives); perf-canary can override. - This PR does not change perf-canary wiring; that will land in perf-canary PR-288. Test plan: - Ran locally in staging harness (A100 8x, H100 8x) with baseline runtime (no fixes) to validate artifact emission + classification. - Validated that non-stalling runs do not produce stall_events and do not regress artifact size. - Added unit tests for watchdog state machine and artifact schema validation. Follow-ups: - Once runtime adds per-rank progress counters as first-class metrics, we should switch from log parsing to metric scraping for better signal quality (tracked in ENG-2404).
commits: scenarios: add tp_hang scenario pack (overload, streaming cancel, rank lag injection)
runner: implement stall watchdog + classification heuristics
artifacts: emit progress.csv + summary.json + stall_events.jsonl bundle
tests: watchdog state machine + artifact schema validation
docs: tp_hang scenarios README + troubleshooting notes
conversation: Marcus Reed (review): Can you clarify how we avoid false positives for long prompts / long decode tails? We’ve seen some requests legitimately have >60s gap between completions on mixed workloads. Isabella Rossi (author): Good call. I adjusted the watchdog to primarily use per-rank progress (heartbeat) when available; completion gap is only used as a secondary signal when progress is also flat. I also changed defaults: stall-timeout-s=180 and added progress-granularity-ms to smooth jitter. Added a note in docs recommending lower thresholds only for canary runs with controlled prompts. Grace Kim (review): For rank_lag_injection, can we make sure we’re not relying on an env var that doesn’t exist in Hosted? Also, please ensure the injection is no-op unless explicitly enabled. Isabella Rossi (author): Updated scenario to require explicit flag --enable-fault-injection and to record injection status in summary.json. Without the flag, the scenario exits early with “skipped” rather than “pass” to avoid giving a false sense of coverage. Omar El-Sayed (review): Artifact format looks good. Can we include a pointer to the related runtime dashboard panels/metrics so oncall can correlate? Even a freeform field in summary.json is fine. Isabella Rossi (author): Added summary.json fields: related_linear, runbook_links, and optional dashboard_hint (string). Kept it purely informational so it won’t break schema validation. Sahana Iyer (review): perf-canary will consume summary.json; please keep the schema stable and versioned. Also, avoid embedding nested objects since our ingestion expects flat key/value. Isabella Rossi (author): Added schema_version=v1 and made summary.json keys strictly top-level scalars. The artifact emitter now asserts no nested structures. Also added tests for schema stability. Marcus Reed (follow-up): Can we get a small snippet in the PR description showing how the classification works? Isabella Rossi (author): Added a short explanation in docs/README instead; PR description was getting too long. Sahana Iyer (approval): LGTM after the schema versioning change. Grace Kim (approval): Looks good. Please keep the “skipped” behavior; that will help avoid silent non-coverage. Omar El-Sayed (approval): Approved. Nice to have consistent artifacts.
release_notes: Benchmark lab now includes TP hang repro scenario definitions and emits standardized stall detection artifacts (summary.json, progress.csv, stall_events.jsonl) to speed up triage and enable perf-canary gating.
